solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bloke, when past his prime, diversified

parts.note: 'if' and 'when' can both introduce a condition
someone past their prime is old

explanation.surface: A man who has gone into new lines of business once his best years were behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloke' is British for a man, and 'when past his prime' splits into two pieces, not one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifold means having many varied forms or parts, which is what diversified describes.

clue.text: Little time for tiny meeting note

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sixty seconds, a short while
second meaning, pronounced my-NEWT: very small
third meaning: the written record of a meeting

explanation.surface: A short slot set aside for a brief note at a small meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings of one spelling: a unit of time, the adjective for very small, and the record kept of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sixty-second span, means extremely small as an adjective, and as a noun is an entry in the official record of proceedings.

clue.text: Manage rising group of childcare centres

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
a series is a group of related things

explanation.surface: Someone is put in charge of a growing chain of childcare businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurseries are places where young children are looked after during the day, so they are childcare centres.

clue.text: Side that's honest? Switch sides!

indicators.note: the two sides are right and left, so the letter for one is swapped for the letter for the other

explanation.surface: A sports-style chant urging a player who changes allegiance to admit which team they really favour.
explanation.walkthrough: In FRANK the R (right) becomes L (left), giving FLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A flank is the side of a body, an army or a building.

clue.text: Left everyone from the South in buy-out of sleep aid

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming from the south means reading upwards, so the word is reversed
in tells us one piece is placed inside another
out here means out of order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A takeover bid presented as something that sends everyone to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buy-out' looks like a takeover, but it is split: the word, then a sign to rearrange it. The upward everyone sits inside that rearrangement, after the leading L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby is a soothing song sung to help a child fall asleep.

clue.text: Dresses for sessions at work

definitions.meaning: second meaning: periods of working time

explanation.surface: A dress code for working hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a loose straight-cut dress and also a scheduled period of work, as in a night shift.

clue.text: Speaking of nosh, the wrong way is to support meat and fast food

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it
going the wrong way means running backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of
nosh and grub are both slang for food

explanation.surface: A food critic complaining that a meat dish is propped up the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaking of' looks like conversational filler but means 'concerning'. Nosh is British slang for food; in a down entry the turned-round piece sits beneath the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamburger is a beef patty in a bun, the standard item sold in fast-food outlets.

clue.text: Confused footballers with the last letter

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, English football's governing body
zed is the British name for Z, the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Players left bewildered when handed the final letter of a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Fazed means disconcerted or thrown off balance, a synonym of confused.

clue.text: Team I would back, quiet as vegetables?

indicators.note: back tells us to read the contraction from end to start

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A fan backing a team that is as subdued as a plate of vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like supporting the team, but it turns the contraction round. The question mark flags vegetables as an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetables are a typical accompaniment served alongside a main course, which is what a side dish is.

clue.text: Regularly annoy jolly friend in the usual way

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually irritates a cheerful pal, as they always do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the friend, but it is a crossword name for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Normally is an adverb meaning as is customary or typical, which is doing something in the usual way.

clue.text: Stunned by a whacky adoption of a non-binary pronoun

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: ze is a gender-neutral pronoun used by some non-binary people

explanation.surface: Someone shocked at a silly move to adopt new pronouns.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first 'a' is wordplay; the second is just the article before the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazed means overwhelmed with surprise, close in sense to stunned.

clue.text: Saint Jude at heart a macho type

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so only the central letters are kept

explanation.surface: A tough-guy portrait of the apostle St Jude.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a virile, sexually confident man, so a macho type.

clue.text: At first, the feeble make only minor changes

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the next word only

explanation.surface: A political jibe that the timid only ever propose small adjustments.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to adjust something slightly, which is making minor changes.

clue.text: 10 considering zombies after a disappearance

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 10 across, a synonym

indicators.note: once the letter a has disappeared from the word, it is missing from the result

parts.note: as to means considering or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone stunned while thinking about zombies after a person goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: AS TO + UNDEAD with its A removed gives ASTOUNDED; the definition is the answer to 10 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Astounded and amazed both mean overwhelmed with surprise, so either can stand for the other.

clue.text: The temperature of a Swedish sauna could be right

definitions.text: The temperature of a Swedish sauna
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a typical sauna heat on the Celsius scale
second meaning: the size of a right angle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' seems to confirm the sauna fact, but it is the angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Saunas typically run at around that Celsius reading, and a right angle measures exactly that many units of turn.

clue.text: Raising status with flashy neon and gaudy jewellery

indicators.note: something flashy is showy and dazzling, telling us these letters are thrown about

parts.note: bling is slang for showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Bright signs and glittering jewels used to look more important.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennobling means making someone noble or more dignified, so raising their status.

clue.text: See 14
Perhaps Memphis follows Europe? That's putting it mildly

definitions.note: a phrase describing a euphemism rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: one piece coming after another sets the order of the pieces
perhaps signals a possible version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tour itinerary: Memphis after Europe, which is an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism is a mild word substituted for a blunt one, so saying it puts things mildly.

clue.text: The man's back, wearing a strange cloak with double end opening

indicators.note: back tells us to read the pronoun from end to start
something worn is surrounded by the garment, so one piece goes inside another
strange means odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

explanation.surface: A man in an odd double-ended cloak, glimpsed from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double end' looks like a feature of the cloak but means the final letter of 'double'. Cakehole is British slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cakehole is a slang word for the mouth, the opening in the face.

clue.text: As nice as can be, drinking right poison

indicators.note: something drinking takes it inside, so one piece goes within the others
as can be suggests whatever arrangement is possible, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cosy picture of someone perfectly pleasant while having the right drink, with a hidden menace.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a whole sentence about niceness; the definition is only the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notoriously toxic element, long the classic poisoner's choice.

clue.text: For a start, come help us, my friend

indicators.note: a start is the beginning, so the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these words

explanation.surface: A plea for help addressed to a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' does double duty, giving the last letter and sitting before 'friend' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Chum is an informal word for a close friend or pal.

clue.text: Band's tour is from the the 5th of August to the 2nd of September

indicators.note: running from one point to another sets the pieces as start, middle and end
the 5th of picks out only the fifth letter of the following word
the 2nd of picks out only the second letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rock band's touring dates, running from early August into September.
explanation.walkthrough: The tour sits between the two selected letters, as the dates bracket a tour. The doubled 'the' is as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow band of colour, as on a flag or shirt.

clue.text: Composer in Paris met an artist

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the run of words that follows

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word into the next three

explanation.surface: A meeting in Paris between a musician and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Smetana was a Czech composer, best known for Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana is a famous nineteenth-century Czech composer, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Container over there in valley

parts.note: yon is an old word for that one over there

explanation.surface: Directions to a container lying in a valley over yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep, steep-sided gorge, a kind of valley.

clue.text: Spread mostly rejected, with awkward true words of one betrayed

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read in reverse
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone betrayed who has seen their claims dismissed and twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: BUTTER loses its last letter, then turns round. 'Et tu, Brute?' is Caesar's reproach to Brutus in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar speaks this Latin phrase on seeing his friend Brutus among his assassins, the classic cry of someone betrayed.

clue.text: Mexican food? Thanks! Served with lettuce

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
cos is a variety of lettuce, also called romaine

explanation.surface: A diner thanking a waiter for Mexican food that came with salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are folded tortillas with fillings, a staple Mexican dish; the question mark marks them as one example.

clue.text: Falstaff, for one, is somewhat uncooperative

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only a portion of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's fat knight Falstaff being a little difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff looks like the character, but here it is Verdi's last work.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff is the title of Verdi's final work for the stage, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Arab coming up soon

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: in a mo is British informal for in a moment, soon

explanation.surface: An Arab visitor who will be arriving shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani, a person from Oman on the Arabian Peninsula, is an Arab.

clue.text: In other words, rebuked for a bloomer

parts.note: or introduces an alternative way of saying something
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: Someone told off for a blunder, a bloomer being a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer is British for an embarrassing mistake, but here it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flowering plant, and a bloomer in the cryptic sense is anything that flowers.

clue.text: Jane's great misfortune?

parts.note: surface reading: a disaster that befell a woman named Jane
setter's reading: the nickname of the Wild West frontierswoman Martha Jane Canary, which is also a word for a great misfortune

explanation.walkthrough: The word sits before Jane in the famous frontierswoman's nickname and on its own means a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster or great misfortune, and it is also the first half of the Wild West heroine's nickname.

clue.text: Flag dodgy engines that won't start

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or faulty, so these letters are rearranged
failing to start means losing the beginning, so the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A warning to mark faulty motors that will not fire up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a verb meaning to mark, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, especially one flown by a ship to show its nationality.

clue.text: Charm of Thailand's first wild animals

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the country's name only
wild means untamed and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The appeal of Thailand's leading wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' looks like appeal, but it is an amulet.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck or protection, which is what a charm is.
